Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.    I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

TY MATTHEWS, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)
Rock Hill, SC • (704) 999-3605 • Matthewstydsw27@gmail.com

October 27, 2026
Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, NC

Re: Clinic Director: Adolescent Mental Health | Launch AWA North Carolina

Dear Hiring Committee:
I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT
Kings Mountain, NC
(704) 418-2440 | celditz@gmail.com

October 26, 2026

Hiring Committee
Launch AWA NC
Re: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health position with Launch AWA NC. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with more than 25 years of experience in clinical and child-and-family services, including over 15 years in program and clinical leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise, operational management, staff development, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for children, adolescents, and families. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. I value collaborative leadership, clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and creating an environment where clinicians feel supported in their work and equipped to provide the highest quality of care.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to serving children and families, particularly those impacted by trauma and other significant life challenges. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my experience to Launch AWA NC and help strengthen mental health services for adolescents. Given my extensive experience, clinical background, and leadership responsibilities, I would also welcome a conversation about compensation. I recognize that the position has a posted salary range; however, I am seeking compensation above that range that more fully reflects my qualifications and the value I would bring to the role. I hope there may be flexibility to discuss a package that aligns with my experience and the position’s responsibilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, leadership experience, and commitment to serving adolescents and families could contribute to the continued success of Launch AWA NC.

Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

I’m excited to apply for the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Mental Health position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I’m interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to build on my experience while contributing to a program that supports adolescents and their families.

Behavioral health professional with experience across ABA, child welfare, and healthcare, bringing a strong foundation in client support, staff development, program coordination, and safety-focused practices. Skilled in training and supporting team members, coordinating with families and multidisciplinary professionals, maintaining accurate documentation, and managing competing priorities in fast-paced environments. Experienced in responding to behavioral challenges, navigating sensitive situations, and promoting consistency and accountability in service delivery. Holds a master’s degree in Special Education with an ABA concentration and a graduate certificate in Contemporary Theory in Mental Health Services, and is pursuing a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a concentration in child and adolescent counseling. Passionate about supporting effective program operations and creating structured, compassionate environments where adolescents and their families can thrive, while ensuring staff feel supported, empowered, and equipped to provide quality care.

Cover Letter: 

Dear Hiring Team,

I was excited to come across the Program Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy because it brings together several areas that have shaped my professional experience and career goals: behavioral health, team development, and supporting children and families. Through my work in ABA and child welfare, I have seen how much of a difference a well-organized, supportive environment can make in a young person's progress. I would love the opportunity to build on that experience by helping lead a program where compassionate care, clear expectations, and strong daily operations work together to support adolescents and their families.

Throughout my nearly five years in ABA, I have gained hands-on experience supporting children and families while helping ensure treatment programs are implemented consistently and effectively. In my role as a Student Analyst, I participated in client intakes and initial assessments, contributed to reassessments and treatment planning, reviewed clinical documentation and behavioral data, and supported parent training and collaboration with multidisciplinary providers. I also helped train and support RBTs, communicate expectations, and work through challenges that affected treatment implementation. These responsibilities taught me the importance of clear communication, staff accountability, consistency, and attention to detail, all of which I recognize as essential to managing daily operations in a PHP/IOP setting.

My experience as a Child Protective Investigator with the State of Florida further strengthened my ability to respond calmly to challenging situations, gather and document sensitive information, assess safety concerns, and communicate with families experiencing difficult circumstances. This role required sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to navigate competing priorities while remaining focused on the well-being of children. I believe these skills would translate well to supporting adolescents with behavioral and emotional needs, responding to unexpected challenges, and helping maintain a safe, structured program environment.

I also bring experience in healthcare administration, including insurance verification, client communication, and managing responsibilities in a fast-paced environment. Combined with my clinical documentation and coordination experience, this background has prepared me to approach operational responsibilities with organization, follow-through, and an understanding of how administrative processes affect the overall client experience. I understand that effective program operations require more than keeping schedules and tasks on track. They require a team that communicates well, understands expectations, follows established procedures, and works together to provide consistent care to clients and their families. I value creating a workplace where staff feel supported and equipped to succeed while also understanding the importance of accountability, collaboration, and maintaining high standards of care.

My educational background reflects my continued commitment to understanding and supporting children, adolescents, and families. I hold a master's degree in Special Education with a concentration in Applied Behavior Analysis, a graduate certificate in Contemporary Theory in Mental Health Services, and a bachelor's degree in Interdisciplinary Social Science with a concentration in Sociology and a minor in Psychology. I am also pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a concentration in child and adolescent counseling. These experiences have reinforced my interest in the connection between behavioral, emotional, and environmental factors and the importance of creating supportive systems around the individuals we serve.

I would be excited to bring my experience, work ethic, and passion for this field to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I take pride in being dependable, thoughtful, and solutions-focused, and I value creating environments where adolescents and families receive compassionate support and staff members feel encouraged to grow and do their best work. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that is committed to helping adolescents and their families navigate challenges, build skills, and make meaningful progress.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with the needs of your program.

Warm regards,
Josmari Arroyo

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear hiring manager, 

I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in working at AWA. With my dedicated background in exceptional student education, passion for inclusive learning, strong ability to collaborate with parents,  and yoga experience, a  I am eager to help students reach their full, social and emotional potential.
My commitment to fostering a supportive and diverse learning atmosphere deeply resonates with my professional philosophy, as well as my ability to speak Portuguese and Spanish. As an ESE Educator, I understand that successful inclusion requires designing and implementing creative accommodations, utilizing assistive technologies, and breaking down complex tasks into manageable milestones for young learners.
During my previous tenure in exceptional student education, I successfully managed a caseload of students with diverse learning needs, including autism spectrum disorder, speech and language impairments, and specific learning disabilities. A key strength I bring  is my collaborative approach to co-teaching and consultation. 
Beyond classroom instruction, I am deeply committed to maintaining transparent, compassionate communication with families. I view parents as essential partners in the education process. Additionally, I am highly skilled in tracking behavioral data and working alongside the team to promote student growth.
I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills, energy, and dedication to equity in education can support your team of adolescents. Thank you for your time,

Sincerely, 

Rosimar Burke

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m writing to express my interest in the Yoga Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy in Coconut Creek. I’m an experienced yoga teacher with a Master of Science in Yoga Therapy and one year of clinical experience working with adult clients. I’ve also taught yoga through Unity for Teens at several high schools in Broward County. Across these settings, I’ve adapted my approach to meet participants’ varied needs and abilities.
I’m drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents in a care setting. My yoga therapy training has prepared me to offer thoughtful, accessible practices that can encourage body awareness, emotional regulation, and a sense of grounding—while respecting each participant’s comfort, boundaries, and readiness. I aim to create a welcoming, nonjudgmental space where students can participate in ways that feel safe and appropriate for them.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience and compassionate, adaptable teaching style to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how I could contribute to the wellness of the adolescents you serve.

Sincerely,
Karen Aylor

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I bring extensive experience in human services and criminal justice, including work as a Probation and Parole Officer and Criminal Court Liaison. Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals navigating the court system, addiction recovery, mental health challenges, and rehabilitation, developing a strong commitment to helping people overcome barriers and achieve positive change.

As a Certified Peer Recovery Specialist and Certified MRT Facilitator, I have experience conducting assessments, coordinating rehabilitation services, developing and monitoring treatment plans, coaching and mentoring individuals, and connecting clients with appropriate services. I am skilled in building productive relationships while maintaining professional boundaries, confidentiality, ethical standards, and respect for all parties involved.

My criminal justice background also includes experience in criminal, family, and juvenile court proceedings. I have prepared and filed court documents, including warrants, violation of probation reports, affidavits, subpoenas, motions, responses, and permanency plans. I am also experienced in courtroom testimony, conflict management, legal procedures, and coordinating services among individuals and agencies.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my combination of criminal justice knowledge, behavioral health experience, communication skills, and commitment to helping others to your organization. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your team.

I believe these principles are particularly important when working with adolescents, who need guidance, encouragement, structure, and the opportunity to develop healthy coping skills.

Throughout my career, I have been committed to advocating for individuals who need support and helping them access the services necessary to improve their lives. Sincerely,  

Carmen Denton

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Program Director role for your Virtual IOP. I live in Naples and am completing a dual Master of Social Work and Master of Science in Criminology at the University of Nebraska Omaha. Building a virtual program that gets adolescents and their families real behavioral health support is exactly the kind of work I want to lead.

My background is in operations leadership. As Director of Operations for The Photography Concierge, I managed 8 locations and a remote team of 15+ staff, wrote the standard operating procedures that kept service consistent, and led the organization's response through the start of the COVID-19 pandemic. Most recently I managed a large global remote team at Orion Photo Group, where I hired, trained, and mentored staff, built onboarding programs, and brought in new technology to scale operations. I'm comfortable owning targets, reporting on results, and building relationships with partners, and I've worked fully remote for years. My graduate training adds a trauma-informed, strengths-based clinical lens, including co-occurring mental health and substance use.

I want to be upfront about two things. My leadership experience is in operations rather than behavioral health specifically, and I'm seeking a practicum placement for my MSW field hours beginning spring 2027. I'd welcome a conversation about whether this role, or another role on your team, could also serve as an employment-based practicum.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Alexandra (Lexi) Korganoff
